question: Why does the word probiotic on a yoghurt label say almost nothing about what it will do?
answer: Because effects belong to particular strains, not to the word. Experts define a probiotic as a live microbe that, in adequate amounts, gives a health benefit, and that proof is usually for one strain at one dose. Two products called probiotic can differ like two pills that are both called medicine.
move: A category name promises less than the specific thing that was tested.
ask: When I buy something for my health, do I know which exact version was shown to work?
source: Hill et al., Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol, 2014
reference: Hill C, Guarner F, Reid G et al., Expert consensus document: the International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics consensus statement on the scope and appropriate use of the term probiotic, Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology, 2014
